title: Composition of product components
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $S,T$ be subsets of its coordinate set, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product outcome space. At every outcome $x$, the $S$-component of the function given by the $T$-component of $f$ equals the $S$-component of $f$ if $S=T$, and equals zero otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of finite probability spaces
each coordinate atom has strictly positive mass
$S,T$ are subsets of the coordinate set
$f$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $S,T\subseteq[n]$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$. The $S$-component of $f_T$ equals $f_S(x)$ when $S=T$, and equals zero otherwise.
